title: Cataloging images
text:
Warning



Documentation is currently incomplete but should be enough to get you started.
Key points:

title: Cataloging images
text:
Example: minimum catalog
Image catalogs must include the following columns:
path|caption|credits|license|tags

paths are relative to the catalog file
tags are comma-separated labels for filtering images

path|caption|credits|license|tags
leiden-pliny/IMG_1200.jpeg|Leiden, MS Lipsius 7  in shelving box, overview of front cover and spine.|Photograph Neel Smith, 2019|Public domain (CC0)|Pliny, Leiden

title: Cataloging images
text:
Example: optional fields
You may optionally include additional columns for year and place.
path|caption|credits|license|tags|year|place
leiden-pliny/IMG_1200.jpeg|Leiden, MS Lipsius 7  in shelving box, overview of front cover and spine.|Photograph Neel Smith, 2019|Public domain (CC0)|Pliny, Leiden, manuscripts|2019|Leiden, NL|

title: Image viewers
text:
The github project at https://github.com/neelsmith/imageviewer hosts apps for light-table and zoomable/pannable display of individual images, implemented in self-contained HTML files that can be run locally or served on the web. Its github pages site hosts an example installation.
The apps support cataloging images in simple delimited-text files, and allow users to filter the light-table display by cataloged data, or by date and location data encoded in the images.

title: Image viewers
text:
Using image viewer apps
image-viewer.html is an app for browsing and viewing images in your local file system. Open it in your favorite web browser, and choose a folder in your local file system. The app will find and images in the folder you are viewing, and allow you to display and filter them just like the web installations.
See this page for information about how to add cataloging information for your local images.
